name: Sludge hauling and landfill; wastewater treatment unit, cement/concrete industry; at plant
description: This unit process reflects sludge hauling to an inert material landfill for U.S. cement and concrete plants. The functional unit reflects sludge management associated with treatment of 1 cubic meter of wastewater from a relevant facility. The scope of this process is limited to sludge hauling to an inert material landfill. Use the corresponding wastewater treatment process to reflect the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts.
category: 56: Administrative and Support and Waste Management and Remediation Services/5622: Waste Treatment and Disposal

processDocumentation.timeDescription: LCI data was developed in CAPDETWorks software to reflect the period from 2014-2019. Updating background electricity and input data should maintain process relevance so long as the target treatment system matches the defined system.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: Basic infrastructure for sludge storage and loading terminal. Sludge is hauled to a landfill in single unit truck.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: Inventory data was generated for a 10 MGD (million gallons per day) theoretical wastewater treatment facility using the CAPDETWorks software package (maintained by Hydromantis). Inventory exchange values were scaled to the quantity of sludge generated per m3 of cement wastewater as compared to the municipal wastewater in the cited EPA report. Background data sources have, in some cases, been updated to reflect newer and/or public data sources.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription: Mechanical and electrical equipment is outside of the scope of this process. Landfilling of cement sludge is modeled using a CUTOFF flow due to the lack of an a suitable available process.  CAPDET works balances mass to model effluent quality and sludge quantity. However, across the entire linked product system a mass balance was not calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: All outputs of the CAPDET model that could be used to develop LCI data were included in the model.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Outputs of the CAPDET model are reported on an annual (energy, chemicals) or lifetime (infrastructure) basis. Annual quantities are standardized to the functional unit by dividing by the average quantity of wastewater treated per year. For inventory data reported on a lifetime basis, quantities are standardized to the functional unit by amortizing the inventory item over the expected lifespan of the infrastructure component.
processDocumentation.samplingDescription: The scope of this treatment process includes basic infrastructure (at the WWTP) and transport of sludge to a landfill (with backhaul). Infrastructure disposal is outside the system boundaries. Landfill disposal of sludge is modeled using a CUTOFF flow due to the absence of a suitable process. Uncertainty ranges are provided on all flows based on the range of dried sludge (following dewatering) that was estimated to be produced per m3 of wastewater (0.12-0.6 kg sludge/m3 wastewater).
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process reflects only the impact of a single wastewater treatment process.  Use one of the corresponding wastewater treatment systems to model the full scope of wastewater treatment impacts.
processDocumentation.intendedApplication: This process is intended to be used as a background process by LCA practitioners, industry and the general public to model wastewater treatment plant construction and operation. This process needs to be used in combination with other wastewater treatment processes, sludge management processes and an effluent release process to model the full scope of wastewater impacts. The inventory should be sufficient to model TRACI 2.1 impact categories.
processDocumentation.projectDescription: Data were prepared by Eastern Research Group (ERG) on behalf of the U.S. EPA under Contract No. EP-C-14-022 WA 1-11, "LCA and Cost Assessment of Nutrient Removal Technologies"
